discovery: The unitarity method and modern on-shell techniques for computing scattering amplitudes in gauge theory and gravity

nominees.name: Lance J. Dixon
nominees.affiliation: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Stanford University

nominees.name: David A. Kosower
nominees.affiliation: Institut de Physique Théorique, CEA Saclay

subfield: Theoretical particle physics / quantum field theory
motivation: Bern, Dixon and Kosower showed that scattering amplitudes can be built directly from their physical singularities, using unitarity and factorization of on-shell amplitudes instead of Feynman diagrams. Their unitarity method broke the computational bottleneck of perturbative QCD, making possible the next-to-leading-order predictions for multi-jet, vector-boson and Higgs production that underpin essentially every LHC measurement and search, including the Higgs discovery and precision electroweak tests. Beyond this practical triumph, their work revealed astonishing hidden simplicity in quantum field theory: all-loop structures in gauge theory, the double-copy relation between gravity and gauge theory, and a deep reorganization of how we understand locality and unitarity. It launched an entire field that has transformed both collider phenomenology and our conceptual picture of spacetime and quantum mechanics. Few theoretical contributions have so directly enabled experiment while also changing how physicists think about the foundations.
